# Building intelligent systems whose **reasoning can be examined.**

My interests meet at a common boundary: systems must interpret complex signals, make useful decisions, and remain understandable when the evidence is incomplete or the environment changes.

::: {.research-body}
## Visual intelligence and vision-language reasoning

Modern multimodal systems can produce fluent answers while relying on incomplete, misplaced, or weakly grounded evidence. I am interested in the mechanisms and evaluation protocols that distinguish apparent understanding from dependable reasoning.

### Questions

- What information should a vision-language system preserve across a long interaction?
- Which evaluation designs reveal grounding and memory failures rather than hide them?
- How can qualitative failure analysis become a reproducible experimental method?

### Current methods

Dataset construction · controlled ablations · benchmark design · retrieval and memory experiments · model-behavior analysis
:::
:::

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-number}
02

::: {.research-body}
## Trustworthy AI and security

Reliability is not a single score. It includes robustness to adversarial inputs, integrity of the evidence chain, privacy-aware system design, and the ability to explain why a result should—or should not—be trusted.

### Questions

- How can we make automated research and reasoning systems resistant to weak or misleading evidence?
- What audit trails are necessary for humans to challenge a model-assisted conclusion?
- Where do security assumptions break when multiple models, tools, and data sources interact?

### Current methods

Threat modeling · adversarial evaluation · provenance tracking · reproducibility checks · evidence-first agent workflows
:::
:::

::: {.research-line}
::: {.research-number}
03
:::

::: {.research-body}
## Quantitative machine learning

Forecasting matters only in relation to a decision. I explore models and interfaces that make uncertainty, scenario sensitivity, and downside risk visible instead of reducing the problem to a single point estimate.

### Questions

- How should a decision system communicate uncertainty without creating false precision?
- Which stress tests reveal fragility in learned financial or operational models?
- How can simulation and machine learning complement one another in decision support?

### Current methods

Time-series modeling · Monte Carlo simulation · scenario analysis · uncertainty estimation · interactive decision support
:::
:::

::: {.research-note}
